title: The Comprehensive List of AI Evaluation Tools

tools.name: Confident AI
tools.description: Confident AI is the AI quality platform built for enterprise platform teams to standardize evals and observability across the org — one consistent bar for how different product teams measure and monitor their AI. Docs

tools.name: Braintrust
tools.description: Braintrust is an eval-first AI engineering platform with experiments, datasets, a prompt playground, logging, and online scoring using its open-source autoevals scorers.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.description: LangSmith is LangChain's platform for tracing, dataset-based evaluation, annotation queues, and prompt management; it works with or without the LangChain framework. Docs

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Langfuse is an open-source, self-hostable LLM engineering platform with tracing, LLM-as-a-judge and custom evaluations, prompt management, datasets, and dashboards. GitHub

tools.name: Arize AX
tools.description: Arize AX is an enterprise AI observability and evaluation platform; its open-source foundation, Phoenix, is listed separately under observability.

tools.name: Opik
tools.description: Opik, from Comet, is an open-source platform to debug, evaluate, and monitor LLM applications, RAG systems, and agents, with tracing, evaluation metrics, datasets, and dashboards. GitHub

tools.name: Galileo
tools.description: Galileo is an enterprise evaluation and observability platform with proprietary evaluation models (e.g., Luna), agent evaluations, guardrailing, and production monitoring.

tools.name: Patronus AI
tools.description: Patronus AI is an automated AI evaluation and testing platform with proprietary evaluators (Lynx for hallucination detection, the Glider judge model), red teaming, and monitoring APIs.

tools.name: Weights & Biases Weave
tools.description: W&B Weave is a tracing and evaluation toolkit for LLM applications with scorers, comparisons, leaderboards, and production monitoring. GitHub

tools.name: Vellum
tools.description: Vellum is a platform for building and evaluating LLM workflows with test suites, side-by-side comparisons, and deployment monitoring.

tools.name: HoneyHive
tools.description: HoneyHive is an AI observability and evaluation platform with tracing, offline and online evaluators, dataset curation, and human review.

tools.name: Maxim AI
tools.description: Maxim AI provides end-to-end simulation, evaluation, and observability for AI agents, including prompt experiments, agent simulation runs, and production quality checks.

tools.name: Freeplay
tools.description: Freeplay combines prompt management, evaluation, and observability with human-in-the-loop review workflows for product teams.

tools.name: Athina AI
tools.description: Athina AI is a collaborative platform to prototype, evaluate, and monitor LLM applications, with a spreadsheet-style experimentation UI and preset plus custom evals.

tools.name: Orq.ai
tools.description: Orq.ai is a generative AI collaboration platform with built-in experiments, evaluators, guardrails, and deployment management.

tools.name: Agenta
tools.description: Agenta is an open-source LLMOps platform with a prompt playground, versioning, human and automatic evaluation, and observability. GitHub

tools.name: LangWatch
tools.description: LangWatch is an open-source platform for LLM evaluation, agent simulation testing (Scenario), and observability. GitHub

tools.name: Openlayer
tools.description: Openlayer provides testing and monitoring for AI systems (LLM and classic ML), with automated tests in CI and production quality alerts.

tools.name: PromptLayer
tools.description: PromptLayer offers prompt management and evaluation: a visual prompt registry, batch evals, A/B testing, and usage analytics.

tools.name: Giskard Hub
tools.description: Giskard Hub is an enterprise agent-testing platform built on the open-source Giskard library, adding vulnerability scanning, continuous red teaming, and business-failure detection.

tools.name: Scale GenAI Platform
tools.description: Scale AI's GenAI platform provides enterprise model evaluation and a data engine, including expert human evaluation and the SEAL leaderboards.

tools.name: DeepEval
tools.description: DeepEval is an open-source LLM evaluation framework ("Pytest for LLMs") with 50+ metrics for RAG, agents, multi-turn conversations, safety, and custom criteria, plus CI/CD and benchmark support.

tools.name: Ragas
tools.description: Ragas is an evaluation toolkit for LLM applications, best known for reference-free RAG metrics such as faithfulness, answer relevancy, and context precision/recall. Paper

tools.name: promptfoo
tools.description: promptfoo is a developer-first CLI for testing prompts, models, and RAG/agent applications, with declarative test cases, comparison matrices, CI integration, and red teaming.

tools.name: OpenAI Evals
tools.description: OpenAI Evals is OpenAI's original open-source framework and registry of community-contributed evals; the repository is in maintenance mode, and OpenAI's separate hosted Evals product is scheduled for shutdown in late 2026.

tools.name: openai/simple-evals
tools.description: simple-evals contains OpenAI's lightweight reference implementations of its reported benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA, SimpleQA, HumanEval, HealthBench, and more).

tools.name: lm-evaluation-harness
tools.description: EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness is a widely used harness for few-shot LLM benchmarking with hundreds of academic tasks; it powered the Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard.

tools.name: Inspect AI
tools.description: Inspect AI is the UK AI Security Institute's framework for LLM evaluations, with solvers, scorers, sandboxed tool use, and agent evals. See also Inspect Evals, a community repository of ready-to-run benchmark implementations. Docs

tools.name: HELM
tools.description: HELM (Holistic Evaluation of Language Models), from Stanford CRFM, provides transparent, reproducible, multi-metric model evaluation. Paper

tools.name: OpenCompass
tools.description: OpenCompass is a large-scale evaluation platform supporting 100+ datasets and a wide range of open and API models.

tools.name: LightEval
tools.description: LightEval is Hugging Face's all-in-one LLM evaluation toolkit across multiple backends (transformers, vLLM, inference endpoints); Hugging Face recommends it over the older Evaluate library for LLM work.

tools.name: Pydantic Evals
tools.description: Pydantic Evals is the evaluation library from the Pydantic team for scoring LLM and agent outputs with datasets, evaluators, and reports. GitHub

tools.name: MLflow LLM Evaluate
tools.description: MLflow's GenAI evaluation module provides heuristic and LLM-judge metrics integrated with MLflow experiment tracking and tracing. GitHub

tools.name: NeMo Evaluator
tools.description: NVIDIA NeMo Evaluator is an open-source platform for scalable, reproducible evaluation of LLMs across popular benchmarks.

tools.name: Prompt flow
tools.description: Microsoft Prompt flow is a development suite for LLM apps that includes built-in and custom evaluation flows for quality assessment in CI.

tools.name: Evidently
tools.description: Evidently is an open-source evaluation and monitoring library for ML and LLM systems with 100+ metrics, test suites, and reports, plus the commercial Evidently Cloud.

tools.name: TruLens
tools.description: TruLens provides evaluation and tracking for LLM apps using feedback functions, and originated the "RAG triad" (context relevance, groundedness, answer relevance).

tools.name: OpenEvals
tools.description: OpenEvals is LangChain's collection of ready-made evaluators for correctness, conciseness, hallucination, and structured output.

tools.name: Evalite
tools.description: Evalite is a TypeScript-native eval runner built on Vitest that treats evals as tests, with a local UI.

tools.name: Giskard
tools.description: Giskard is an open-source testing library for LLM agents and ML models with automatic vulnerability scanning for hallucination, bias, and injection.

tools.name: EvalScope
tools.description: EvalScope is ModelScope's framework for LLM/VLM/AIGC evaluation and inference performance benchmarking.

tools.name: OLMES
tools.description: OLMES is AI2's reproducible standard for LLM evaluations, used for the OLMo and Tülu model reports.

tools.name: Eureka ML Insights
tools.description: Eureka ML Insights is Microsoft's framework for standardized, reproducible evaluation of large foundation models.

tools.name: Weave Evaluations
tools.description: Weave Evaluations is W&B Weave's code-first evaluation harness with scorers, datasets, and model comparisons.

tools.name: LLM Comparator
tools.description: LLM Comparator, from Google's PAIR team, is an interactive tool for side-by-side analysis of LLM evaluation results.

tools.name: Parea
tools.description: Parea's SDK provides experiment tracking and evaluation for LLM applications.

tools.name: continuous-eval
tools.description: continuous-eval, from Relari, offers data-driven, modular evaluation for LLM pipelines with metric ensembles. Repository activity has slowed since early 2025.

tools.name: Phoenix Evals
tools.description: Phoenix Evals is Arize Phoenix's evaluation library with pre-tested LLM-judge templates for hallucination, relevance, toxicity, and more.

tools.name: UpTrain
tools.description: UpTrain is an open-source tool to evaluate and improve LLM applications with 20+ preconfigured checks. Repository activity has slowed since 2024.

tools.name: AlpacaEval
tools.description: AlpacaEval is a fast, inexpensive, replicable LLM-based automatic evaluator for instruction-following models.

tools.name: Evalchemy
tools.description: Evalchemy, from ML Foundations, is a unified toolkit for running many popular benchmarks against any model.

tools.name: Evaluate
tools.description: Hugging Face Evaluate is a library of standard NLP/ML metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) with a unified API; it is in maintenance mode, with LightEval recommended for new LLM evaluation work.

tools.name: FastChat
tools.description: FastChat is LMSYS's platform for serving and evaluating chat models, and the original home of MT-Bench and the Chatbot Arena codebase; development has slowed and it is now mostly of historical reference value.

tools.name: Microsoft Foundry Evaluations
tools.description: Microsoft Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) includes built-in evaluators for generative and agentic applications, covering intent resolution, tool-call accuracy, task adherence, groundedness, and safety.

tools.name: Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation
tools.description: Google Cloud's Gen AI Evaluation Service provides model-based and computation-based metrics, including agent trajectory evaluation, integrated with Vertex AI.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations
tools.description: Amazon Bedrock Evaluations runs managed model and RAG evaluation jobs using automatic metrics, LLM-as-a-judge, and human evaluation workflows.

tools.name: Mosaic AI Agent Evaluation
tools.description: Databricks' Mosaic AI Agent Evaluation provides managed judges, a human review app, and MLflow integration for evaluating GenAI apps on Databricks.

tools.name: OpenAI Evals (hosted)
tools.description: OpenAI's platform-integrated evaluation product for testing prompts and models in the OpenAI dashboard; OpenAI has announced a shutdown of the hosted Evals product scheduled for late 2026.

tools.name: Anthropic Console Evaluations
tools.description: The Anthropic Console includes an evaluation tool for generating test cases and comparing prompt outputs for Claude models.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Langfuse is a widely adopted open-source LLM observability platform with traces, sessions, cost tracking, evaluations, and prompt management; it is self-hostable.

tools.name: Arize Phoenix
tools.description: Phoenix is an OpenTelemetry-native tracing and evaluation library for LLM apps and agents that runs locally, in notebooks, or self-hosted; it underpins the commercial Arize AX platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: Helicone is an LLM observability proxy/gateway added with one line of code, providing logging, caching, scoring, and experiments.

tools.name: Opik
tools.description: Opik is Comet's open-source tracing and evaluation platform for LLM and agentic applications.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.description: OpenLLMetry, from Traceloop, provides OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation for LLM apps, exporting traces to any OTel-compatible backend.

tools.name: OpenInference
tools.description: OpenInference is an open specification and set of instrumentation libraries for capturing LLM application traces, used by Phoenix and other OTel backends.

tools.name: OpenLIT
tools.description: OpenLIT is an OpenTelemetry-native AI engineering platform with observability, evaluations, guardrails, and a prompt hub.

tools.name: AgentOps
tools.description: AgentOps provides session replays, metrics, and monitoring purpose-built for AI agents across popular agent frameworks.

tools.name: Laminar
tools.description: Laminar is an open-source, OTel-based platform for tracing and evaluating AI applications.

tools.name: Pydantic Logfire
tools.description: Logfire, from the Pydantic team, is an observability platform with first-class LLM and agent tracing built on OpenTelemetry.

tools.name: Lunary
tools.description: Lunary is a production toolkit for LLM apps covering observability, prompt management, and analytics.

tools.name: Langtrace
tools.description: Langtrace is an open-source, OTel-based observability tool with evaluations for LLM applications.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: Portkey combines an open-source AI gateway with a commercial observability and governance suite: routing, guardrails, logs, and feedback.

tools.name: Datadog LLM Observability
tools.description: Datadog LLM Observability adds LLM tracing, quality and security scanning, and evaluation to the Datadog platform.

tools.name: New Relic AI Monitoring
tools.description: New Relic AI Monitoring provides APM-style monitoring for LLM-powered applications, covering traces, cost, and response quality signals.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.description: LangSmith provides tracing and monitoring with online evaluators and alerts (see the [full-stack platforms](#full-stack-llm-evaluation-platforms) section).

tools.name: Arthur
tools.description: Arthur is an AI performance monitoring platform; its open-source Arthur Bench LLM evaluation tool is no longer actively developed.

tools.name: LangKit
tools.description: LangKit is an open-source library of text-quality and safety telemetry metrics for LLMs, built on whylogs. The hosted WhyLabs platform it fed into has been discontinued (see [Discontinued](#discontinued-and-historical-tools)).

tools.name: Speakeasy AI Control Plane
tools.description: Speakeasy AI Control Plane centrally governs agent and MCP access with role-scoped permissions and auditable records for tool calls.

tools.name: Ragas
tools.description: Ragas is a popular toolkit for RAG metrics: faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall.

tools.name: DeepEval RAG metrics
tools.description: DeepEval's RAG metrics cover answer relevancy, faithfulness, and contextual precision/recall/relevancy, with explainable per-test-case reasons.

tools.name: TruLens
tools.description: TruLens implements RAG triad evaluation (context relevance, groundedness, answer relevance) with application instrumentation.

tools.name: ARES
tools.description: ARES, from Stanford, automates RAG evaluation using synthetic data and fine-tuned judge models with statistical guarantees. Paper

tools.name: AutoRAG
tools.description: AutoRAG is an AutoML-style tool that evaluates RAG pipeline configurations on your own data to find the best-performing setup.

tools.name: RAGChecker
tools.description: RAGChecker, from Amazon Science, is a fine-grained diagnostic framework for RAG using claim-level entailment checks on both retriever and generator.

tools.name: BEIR
tools.description: BEIR is a heterogeneous zero-shot benchmark for information retrieval spanning 18 datasets across 9 task types.

tools.name: MTEB
tools.description: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) is the benchmark suite for evaluating embedding models, with a public leaderboard.

tools.name: CRAG
tools.description: CRAG (Comprehensive RAG Benchmark), from Meta, provides 4,400+ QA pairs and mock APIs simulating web and knowledge-graph search, used in the KDD Cup 2024.

tools.name: RAGBench
tools.description: RAGBench is a 100k-example, explainable RAG benchmark across five industry domains, with the TRACe evaluation framework.

tools.name: BRIGHT
tools.description: BRIGHT is a benchmark for reasoning-intensive retrieval where queries require deep reasoning rather than keyword matching.

tools.name: MTRAG
tools.description: MTRAG, from IBM, is a human-generated benchmark for multi-turn RAG conversations across four domains.

tools.name: Tonic Validate
tools.description: Tonic Validate is a RAG benchmarking and evaluation framework with a free visualization UI.

tools.name: continuous-eval
tools.description: continuous-eval offers modular, granular evaluation of each RAG pipeline stage: retrieval, reranking, and generation.

tools.name: FlashRAG
tools.description: FlashRAG is a Python toolkit for reproducing and evaluating RAG research, with 20+ algorithms and 16+ datasets.

tools.name: RAGTruth
tools.description: RAGTruth is a word-level, hallucination-annotated corpus for training and evaluating trustworthy RAG systems.

tools.name: RGB
tools.description: RGB benchmarks RAG robustness across noise, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactuals.

tools.name: DeepEval agentic evals
tools.description: DeepEval's agentic metrics cover task completion, tool correctness, and argument correctness, supporting end-to-end and component-level agent testing over traces.

tools.name: LangWatch Scenario
tools.description: Scenario, from LangWatch, is an agent simulation testing framework that simulates users over multi-turn scenarios and asserts on outcomes.

tools.name: AgentEvals
tools.description: AgentEvals is LangChain's set of ready-made evaluators for agent trajectories, including trajectory match and LLM-judge over trajectories.

tools.name: Inspect AI
tools.description: Inspect AI has first-class agent evaluation support: sandboxed tool execution, multi-step solvers, and agent bridges.

tools.name: Rogue
tools.description: Rogue, from Qualifire, evaluates and red-teams agents by probing them through realistic adversarial conversations.

tools.name: any-agent
tools.description: any-agent, from Mozilla AI, is a single interface for building and evaluating agents across different agent frameworks.

tools.name: Vivaria
tools.description: Vivaria is METR's platform for running agent evaluations and conducting elicitation research.

tools.name: Harbor
tools.description: Harbor is a framework for running agent evaluations and creating RL environments at scale.

tools.name: ToolSandbox
tools.description: ToolSandbox, from Apple, is a stateful, conversational, interactive evaluation benchmark for LLM tool-use capabilities.

tools.name: Coval
tools.description: Coval is a simulation and evaluation platform for voice and chat agents, applying scenario-based automated testing practices borrowed from self-driving-car simulation.

tools.name: Hamming
tools.description: Hamming automates voice-agent testing at scale with thousands of simulated phone calls, prompt experiments, and production call analytics.

tools.name: Cekura
tools.description: Cekura (formerly Vocera) provides testing and observability for voice and chat agents via simulated conversations and production monitoring.

tools.name: DeepEval conversational metrics
tools.description: DeepEval's conversational metrics evaluate multi-turn conversations at the turn and conversation level (role adherence, knowledge retention, conversation completeness) and include user simulation.

tools.name: Bland AI Testing
tools.description: Bland AI includes built-in test suites for phone-call agents on the Bland platform.

tools.name: MultiChallenge
tools.description: MultiChallenge, from Scale AI, benchmarks realistic multi-turn conversation ability of frontier LLMs.

tools.name: DeepTeam
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: DeepTeam is an open-source LLM red-teaming framework covering 120+ vulnerabilities and 20+ attack methods, with mappings to the OWASP Top 10, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS.

tools.name: garak
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: garak, from NVIDIA, is an LLM vulnerability scanner ("nmap for LLMs") probing hallucination, jailbreaks, toxicity, and data leakage. Paper

tools.name: PyRIT
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: PyRIT is Microsoft's Python Risk Identification Toolkit for generative AI, used by Microsoft's AI Red Team for automated adversarial probing.

tools.name: promptfoo red teaming
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: promptfoo's red-teaming module runs automated scans for injection, jailbreaks, PII leakage, and RBAC issues, with OWASP and NIST mappings.

tools.name: HarmBench
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: HarmBench, from the Center for AI Safety, is a standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming and robust refusal.

tools.name: Giskard scan
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: Giskard's scan feature automatically detects vulnerabilities in LLM agents, including injection, harmful content, and sycophancy.

tools.name: FuzzyAI
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: FuzzyAI, from CyberArk, is an automated LLM fuzzer for discovering jailbreaks and adversarial weaknesses in model guardrails.

tools.name: CyberSecEval
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: CyberSecEval, part of Meta's Purple Llama project, benchmarks LLM cybersecurity risks including insecure code generation and cyberattack helpfulness.

tools.name: Lakera Red
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: Lakera Red is an AI red-teaming service from the team behind the Gandalf prompt-injection game.

tools.name: Mindgard
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: Mindgard is an automated AI red teaming and security testing platform (offensive security for AI systems).

tools.name: HiddenLayer
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: HiddenLayer is an AI security platform covering model scanning and adversarial ML detection and response.

tools.name: Cisco AI Defense
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: Cisco AI Defense, built on the Robust Intelligence acquisition, provides algorithmic red teaming and runtime guardrails for enterprises.

tools.name: Haize Labs
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: Haize Labs provides automated stress-testing/jailbreaking ("haizing") suites and judge infrastructure for frontier AI systems.

tools.name: AgentDojo
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: AgentDojo, from ETH Zurich, is a dynamic environment for evaluating prompt-injection attacks and defenses in tool-using LLM agents.

tools.name: JailbreakBench
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: JailbreakBench is an open robustness benchmark for jailbreaking, with a leaderboard and artifact repository.

tools.name: Moonshot
tools.category: LLM Red Teaming and Security Testing
tools.description: Moonshot, from the AI Verify Foundation, is a modular tool for benchmarking and red-teaming LLM applications.

tools.name: NeMo Guardrails
tools.description: NeMo Guardrails is NVIDIA's toolkit for programmable guardrails (via Colang) on conversational systems: topic control, jailbreak detection, and fact-checking rails.

tools.name: Guardrails AI
tools.description: Guardrails AI is a Python framework for input/output validation, with a community Guardrails Hub of validators.

tools.name: LLM Guard
tools.description: LLM Guard, from Protect AI, is a security toolkit providing sanitization, PII detection, and prompt-injection and toxicity scanners.

tools.name: LlamaFirewall
tools.description: LlamaFirewall, from Meta, is an open-source guardrail framework for agentic systems, combining PromptGuard, agent-alignment checks, and code-safety scanning.

tools.name: OpenAI Guardrails
tools.description: OpenAI Guardrails is a modular safety framework for validating LLM inputs and outputs with configurable pipelines.

tools.name: Invariant Guardrails
tools.description: Invariant, from Invariant Labs, provides guardrailing rules and analysis for agentic systems, including tool-call policy enforcement.

tools.name: Lakera Guard
tools.description: Lakera Guard is a low-latency API for detecting prompt injection, content violations, and PII in production.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
tools.description: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails applies configurable safety policies — content filters, denied topics, and contextual grounding checks — to Bedrock applications.

tools.name: Azure AI Content Safety
tools.description: Azure AI Content Safety provides content moderation plus Prompt Shields (jailbreak and indirect injection detection) and groundedness detection.

tools.name: Google Model Armor
tools.description: Model Armor is Google Cloud's service for screening LLM prompts and responses for injection, jailbreaks, sensitive data, and harmful content.

tools.name: Llama Guard
tools.description: Llama Guard is Meta's family of downloadable safety classifier models (Llama Guard, Prompt Guard) under the Purple Llama project, released under Meta's community license.

tools.name: OpenAI Moderation
tools.description: The OpenAI Moderation endpoint is a free API for text and image safety classification.

tools.name: Vectara HHEM
tools.description: HHEM is Vectara's widely used open hallucination detection model, which powers the Hughes Hallucination Leaderboard.

tools.name: Patronus Lynx
tools.description: Lynx, from Patronus AI, is a hallucination detection model reported to outperform GPT-4 on the HaluBench benchmark (July 2024 paper). Paper

tools.name: SelfCheckGPT
tools.description: SelfCheckGPT performs zero-resource, black-box hallucination detection via sampling consistency. Paper

tools.name: FActScore
tools.description: FActScore provides fine-grained, atomic-fact evaluation of factual precision in long-form generation. Paper

tools.name: LongFact & SAFE
tools.description: LongFact (a long-form factuality benchmark) and SAFE (Search-Augmented Factuality Evaluator), from Google DeepMind, evaluate long-form factuality using search-grounded fact checking.

tools.name: MiniCheck
tools.description: MiniCheck is an efficient fact-checking model for verifying whether LLM output sentences are grounded in provided documents, at a fraction of GPT-4's cost.

tools.name: AlignScore
tools.description: AlignScore is a unified metric for factual-consistency evaluation trained on a broad alignment corpus.

tools.name: FacTool
tools.description: FacTool performs tool-augmented factuality detection across knowledge-based QA, code, math, and scientific review.

tools.name: TruthfulQA
tools.description: TruthfulQA is a benchmark measuring whether models reproduce common human falsehoods. Paper

tools.name: HaluEval
tools.description: HaluEval is a large-scale hallucination evaluation benchmark with 35K samples.

tools.name: HaluBench
tools.description: HaluBench, from Patronus AI, is a hallucination evaluation benchmark of 15K real-world RAG samples spanning finance and medicine.

tools.name: FACTS Grounding
tools.description: FACTS Grounding, from Google DeepMind, is a benchmark and leaderboard for grounding quality in long-form responses.

tools.name: SimpleQA
tools.description: SimpleQA, from OpenAI, benchmarks short-form factuality and serves as a useful hallucination-rate probe. Paper

tools.name: G-Eval
tools.description: G-Eval is a chain-of-thought, form-filling LLM-judging algorithm (Liu et al., 2023); production implementations are available in DeepEval and other frameworks, letting you define custom criteria in plain language.

tools.name: Prometheus 2
tools.description: Prometheus 2 is a family of open judge language models specialized in fine-grained, rubric-based evaluation of other models. Paper

tools.name: Glider
tools.description: Glider, from Patronus AI, is a 3.8B-parameter explainable rubric-based judge model with span-level highlights.

tools.name: Atla Selene
tools.description: Selene, from Atla, is a small judge model family purpose-trained for evaluation tasks.

tools.name: JudgeLM
tools.description: JudgeLM, from BAAI, provides fine-tuned, scalable judge models for open-ended benchmarks.

tools.name: Verdict
tools.description: Verdict, from Haize Labs, is a declarative library for building compound LLM-judge systems: ensembles, debates, and verification chains.

tools.name: judges
tools.description: judges, from Quotient AI, is a small library of curated, research-backed judge prompts.

tools.name: autoevals
tools.description: autoevals, from Braintrust, is a library of automatic evaluators (factuality, closed-QA, RAG scorers) for LLM outputs.

tools.name: PandaLM
tools.description: PandaLM is a reproducible judge model for pairwise LLM comparison.

tools.name: Flow Judge
tools.description: Flow Judge, from Flow AI, is a compact 3.8B-parameter open evaluator model for customizable rubric evaluation.

tools.name: RewardBench
tools.description: RewardBench, from AI2, was the first benchmark for evaluating reward models; RewardBench 2 extends it with harder, unseen human prompts.

tools.name: JudgeBench
tools.description: JudgeBench evaluates LLM-based judges on challenging response pairs spanning knowledge, reasoning, math, and coding.

tools.name: RM-Bench
tools.description: RM-Bench evaluates reward models' sensitivity to subtle content changes and resistance to style bias.

tools.name: LLMBar
tools.description: LLMBar, from Princeton NLP, is a meta-evaluation benchmark testing whether LLM evaluators can detect instruction-following correctly against adversarial distractors.

tools.name: LM-Polygraph
tools.description: LM-Polygraph implements a broad suite of uncertainty-quantification methods for LLM outputs with a unified benchmark.

tools.name: TruthTorchLM
tools.description: TruthTorchLM is an open-source library of truthfulness-prediction and uncertainty methods for generative LLMs.

tools.name: Cleanlab TLM
tools.description: Cleanlab's Trustworthy Language Model (TLM) adds real-time trustworthiness and confidence scores to any LLM output.

tools.name: UQ360
tools.description: Uncertainty Quantification 360, from IBM, is a toolkit for quantifying and communicating uncertainty in machine-learning models.

tools.name: MMLU
tools.description: MMLU is a 57-subject multiple-choice knowledge benchmark that served for years as the default capability probe. Paper

tools.name: MMLU-Pro
tools.description: MMLU-Pro is a harder, more robust successor to MMLU with 10 answer choices and more reasoning-heavy questions.

tools.name: GPQA
tools.description: GPQA is a graduate-level, "Google-proof" science QA benchmark written by domain experts. Paper

tools.name: Humanity's Last Exam
tools.description: Humanity's Last Exam contains 2,500 extremely difficult expert-written questions across 100+ subjects, designed as a "final" closed-ended academic benchmark. Site

tools.name: BIG-bench
tools.description: BIG-bench is a collaborative benchmark of 200+ tasks probing model capabilities and limitations; see also BIG-Bench Hard.

tools.name: GSM8K
tools.description: GSM8K is a benchmark of grade-school math word problems, a classic chain-of-thought reasoning test.

tools.name: MATH
tools.description: MATH contains 12,500 competition mathematics problems.

tools.name: FrontierMath
tools.description: FrontierMath, from Epoch AI, is a private benchmark of exceptionally hard, unpublished research-level math problems.

tools.name: AIME
tools.description: AIME (American Invitational Mathematics Examination) problems are widely used to test frontier-model math, e.g., via MathArena.

tools.name: IFEval
tools.description: IFEval tests verifiable instruction following (e.g., "answer in exactly 3 paragraphs"). Paper

tools.name: MT-Bench
tools.description: MT-Bench is a multi-turn conversation benchmark scored by LLM judges, introduced alongside Chatbot Arena. Paper

tools.name: Arena-Hard
tools.description: Arena-Hard is an automatic benchmark built from challenging live Arena prompts, with high correlation to human preference rankings.
